- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >5% deviation) and sentiment is low (≤0.4), consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.2–0.8), model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; use 3-day moving average of true values as a sanity check.
- For 30-day forecasts, if model shows persistent upward trend with low sentiment, reduce slope by 10–20% to account for market cooling.
- If true outcome is consistently below model (especially in 3rd–5th day of forecast), model may be overreacting to sentiment; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for each day sentiment <0.6.
